     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"
    49	
    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""
    53	MODELINV=""
    54	JSON=0
    55	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"
    74	TOP="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die 2 "not inside a git repository"
    75	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || PLAN="$TOP/grimoires/loa/sprint.md"
    76	[[ -n "$MODELINV" ]] || MODELINV="$TOP/.run/model-invoke.jsonl"
    77	[[ -r "$PLAN" && -f "$PLAN" ]] || die 2 "sprint plan not readable: $PLAN"
    78	[[ -r "$FENCE_AWK" ]] || die 2 "cannot read $FENCE_AWK (reinstall the framework scripts)"
    79	
    80	# A leading '-' would reach git as an option; a SHA never starts with one.
    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac
    82	case "$TO" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $TO" ;; esac
    83	FROM_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${FROM}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM"
    84	TO_SHA="$(git rev-parse --verify --quiet "${TO}^{commit}")" || die 3 "unknown commit: $TO"
    85	
    86	# --- kinds -------------------------------------------------------------------
    87	kinds="$(awk "$(cat "$FENCE_AWK")"'
    88	  md_fence($0) { next }
    89	  /^## / { insp = ($0 ~ /^## Sprint [0-9]/); sec = 0; next }
    90	  !insp { next }
    91	  /^### / {
    92	    sec = 0
    93	    if ($0 ~ /^### Technical Tasks[[:space:]]*$/) sec = 1
    94	    else if ($0 ~ /^### Task [0-9A-Za-z]+\.E2E([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)/) sec = 2
    95	    next
    96	  }
    97	  !sec || $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] / { next }
    98	  sec == 2 && $0 !~ /^- \[[ xX]\] Task / { next }
    99	  {
   100	    if (match($0, /(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])kind[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(mechanical|judgment|operator)[[:space:]]*$/)) {
   101	      v = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH)
   102	      sub(/^.*:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
   103	      n[v]++
   104	    } else n["untagged"]++
   105	  }
   106	  END { printf "%d %d %d %d\n", n["mechanical"], n["judgment"], n["operator"], n["untagged"] }
   107	' "$PLAN")"
   108	read -r K_MECH K_JUDG K_OPER K_UNTAGGED <<< "$kinds"
   109	[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2
   110	
   111	# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
   113	SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
   114	  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"
   115	PROSE_BYTES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --unified=0 "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.md' \
   116	  | awk '
   117	      /^diff --git / { hunk = 0; next }
   118	      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
   119	      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
   120	      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
   121	      END { printf "%d\n", s }
   122	    ')"
   123	
   124	# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
   125	FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
   126	TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
   127	MODEL_CALLS=""
   128	if [[ -f "$MODELINV" && -r "$MODELINV" ]]; then
   129	  MODEL_CALLS="$(jq -R --argjson lo "$FROM_TS" --argjson hi "$TO_TS" '
   130	      fromjson? | select(type == "object" and .primitive_id == "MODELINV")
   131	      | (.ts_utc // "") | tostring
   132	      | (try (sub("\\.[0-9]+"; "") | sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601) catch null)
   133	      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
   134	    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
   135	else
   136	  echo "WARN: MODELINV log not found at $MODELINV; model calls n/a" >&2
   137	fi
   138	
   139	iso() { jq -nr --argjson t "$1" '$t | todateiso8601'; }
   140	
   141	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   142	  jq -n \
   143	    --arg from "$FROM_SHA" --arg to "$TO_SHA" \
   144	    --arg from_ts "$(iso "$FROM_TS")" --arg to_ts "$(iso "$TO_TS")" \
   145	    --arg plan "$PLAN" --arg modelinv "$MODELINV" \
   146	    --argjson mech "$K_MECH" --argjson judg "$K_JUDG" --argjson oper "$K_OPER" --argjson untagged "$K_UNTAGGED" \
   147	    --argjson script_lines "$SCRIPT_LINES" --argjson prose_bytes "$PROSE_BYTES" \
   148	    --arg calls "$MODEL_CALLS" \
   149	    '{from: $from, to: $to, window: {from: $from_ts, to: $to_ts}, sprint_plan: $plan,
   150	      kinds: {mechanical: $mech, judgment: $judg, operator: $oper, untagged: $untagged},
---ARMS-REPORT---
     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""arms-report.py — the cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm report (SDD D-2.3).
     3	
     4	Invoked by `report.sh --arms`. Reads <results-root>/<suite>/STATUS.json (the
     5	suite aggregate run-arms.sh writes), every batch's MANIFEST.json and
     6	<arm>/results.jsonl, and the suite's pre-registered `ab.threshold` and
     7	`ab.arms`, and writes one markdown report.
     8	
     9	Per arm: recall (mean over defect fixtures of the per-fixture trial mean;
    10	the min, max and spread of the per-trial means), refuted share (cited
    11	findings matching neither a feedback label nor a fix region, over cited
    12	findings, pooled over completed trials), tokens per call, the percentile
    13	bootstrap interval of the recall drop (baseline - arm) resampling fixtures,
    14	the verdict and the missed labels.
    15	
    16	Verdict (pre-registered; never computed for baseline):
    17	  inconclusive  --partial; the run is not complete; a planned fixture lacks
    18	                trials_required completed trials in the arm or the baseline;
    19	                model or source skew; no defect fixture; or only a recall
    20	                rule is violated while the mean drop does not exceed the
    21	                baseline's own trial-to-trial spread (a change too small to name)
    22	  recall loss   the refuted-share rule is violated, or a recall rule is
    23	                violated and the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread
    24	  no recall loss  every rule holds:
    25	                  upper bound of the drop interval <= mean_recall_max_drop
    26	                  arm min trial mean >= baseline min trial mean - min_trial_recall_max_drop
    27	                  arm refuted share <= baseline refuted share + refuted_share_max_rise
    28	An `informational: true` arm's verdict reports a yield only.
    29	
    30	Exit: 0 written, 1 refused (a suite is not complete and --partial was not
    31	given), 2 error. Stdlib only.
    32	"""
    33	import argparse
    34	import datetime
    35	import json
    36	import os
    37	import random
    38	import sys
    39	from collections import Counter, defaultdict
    40	
    41	
    42	def load_yaml_subset(path):
    43	    """The suites are YAML (no stdlib parser); the harness already depends on yq v4."""
    44	    import subprocess
    45	    out = subprocess.run(["yq", "-o=json", ".", path], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    46	    return json.loads(out)
    47	
    48	
    49	def read_jsonl(path):
    50	    rows = []
    51	    if not os.path.isfile(path):
    52	        return rows
    53	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    54	        for line in fh:
    55	            line = line.strip()
    56	            if line:
    57	                try:
    58	                    rows.append(json.loads(line))
    59	                except ValueError:
    60	                    continue
    61	    return rows
    62	
    63	
    64	def mean(xs):
    65	    xs = [x for x in xs if x is not None]
    66	    return sum(xs) / len(xs) if xs else None
    67	
    68	
    69	def fmt(x, nd=3):
    70	    return "n/a" if x is None else f"{x:.{nd}f}"
    71	
    72	
    73	def recall_details(row):
    74	    for g in row.get("graders") or []:
    75	        if g.get("name") == "recall-vs-defects.sh" and isinstance(g.get("details"), dict):
    76	            return g["details"]
    77	    return None
    78	
    79	
    80	def tokens(row):
    81	    u = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("usage") or {}
    82	    if not u:
    83	        return None
    84	    return sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
    85	               ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
    86	
    87	
    88	def percentile(sorted_xs, q):
    89	    if not sorted_xs:
    90	        return None
    91	    k = max(0, min(len(sorted_xs) - 1, int(round(q * (len(sorted_xs) - 1)))))
    92	    return sorted_xs[k]
    93	
    94	
    95	def bootstrap(deltas, iterations, level, seed):
    96	    """Percentile bootstrap of the mean of per-fixture deltas (resample fixtures)."""
    97	    if not deltas:
    98	        return None, None
    99	    rng = random.Random(seed)
   100	    n = len(deltas)
   101	    means = sorted(sum(deltas[rng.randrange(n)] for _ in range(n)) / n for _ in range(iterations))
   102	    a = (1.0 - level) / 2.0
   103	    return percentile(means, a), percentile(means, 1.0 - a)
   104	
   105	
   106	class Arm:
   107	    def __init__(self, arm_id):
   108	        self.id = arm_id
   109	        self.cells = defaultdict(list)   # fixture -> [(trial, recall)], every completed trial kept
   110	        self.planted = {}                # fixture -> planted count
   111	        self.cited = 0
   112	        self.refuted = 0
   113	        self.tokens = []
   114	        self.models = set()
   115	        self.sources = set()
   116	        self.done = 0
   117	        self.errors = 0
   118	        self.fallback_trials = 0         # trials the CLI moved to another model on a safeguard refusal
   119	        self.fallback_kinds = Counter()
   120	        self.missed = Counter()          # (fixture, label) -> trials missed
   121	        self.seen = Counter()            # (fixture, label) -> trials graded
   122	
   123	    def add(self, row):
   124	        if row.get("status") != "completed":
   125	            self.errors += 1
   126	            return
   127	        d = recall_details(row)
   128	        if d is None:
   129	            self.errors += 1
   130	            return
   131	        self.done += 1
   132	        fx = row.get("fixture") or row.get("task_id", "").split("-", 1)[-1]
   133	        self.planted[fx] = int(d.get("planted") or 0)
   134	        if d.get("recall") is not None:
   135	            self.cells[fx].append((int(row.get("trial") or 0), float(d["recall"])))
   136	        if d.get("findings_cited") is not None:
   137	            self.cited += int(d.get("findings_cited") or 0)
   138	            self.refuted += int(d.get("findings_refuted") or 0)
   139	        t = tokens(row)
   140	        if t is not None:
   141	            self.tokens.append(t)
   142	        self.models.add(row.get("model_id") or (row.get("executor") or {}).get("model_id"))
   143	        # every model that produced output in the call (an auxiliary model is skew too)
   144	        for mid, out in ((row.get("executor") or {}).get("models_used") or {}).items():
   145	            if out:
   146	                self.models.add(mid)
   147	        fb = (row.get("executor") or {}).get("refusal_fallbacks") or []
   148	        if fb:
   149	            self.fallback_trials += 1
   150	            for x in fb:
   151	                self.fallback_kinds[f"{x.get('from')}→{x.get('to')} ({x.get('category')})"] += 1
   152	        self.sources.add(row.get("source_commit") or (row.get("executor") or {}).get("source_commit"))
   153	        for lbl in d.get("missed") or []:
   154	            self.missed[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   155	            self.seen[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   156	        for lbl in d.get("detected") or []:
   157	            self.seen[(fx, lbl)] += 1
   158	
   159	    def defect_fixtures(self):
   160	        return sorted(f for f, p in self.planted.items() if p > 0 and self.cells.get(f))
   161	
   162	    def fixture_means(self):
   163	        return {f: mean([r for _t, r in self.cells[f]]) for f in self.defect_fixtures()}
   164	
   165	    def trial_means(self):
   166	        by_trial = defaultdict(list)
   167	        for f in self.defect_fixtures():
   168	            for t, r in self.cells[f]:
   169	                by_trial[t].append(r)
   170	        return {t: mean(v) for t, v in sorted(by_trial.items())}
   171	
   172	    def refuted_share(self):
   173	        return self.refuted / self.cited if self.cited else None
   174	
   175	
   176	def suite_report(root, suites_dir, suite, partial, out_lines):
   177	    sdir = os.path.join(root, suite)
   178	    status = {}
   179	    sp = os.path.join(sdir, "STATUS.json")
   180	    if os.path.isfile(sp):
   181	        status = json.load(open(sp, encoding="utf-8"))
   182	    spec = load_yaml_subset(os.path.join(suites_dir, f"{suite}.yaml"))
   183	    ab = spec.get("ab") or {}
   184	    th = ab.get("threshold") or {}
   185	    arm_meta = {a["id"]: a for a in ab.get("arms") or []}
   186	    trials_required = int(th.get("trials_required", 3))
   187	    max_drop = float(th.get("mean_recall_max_drop", 0.10))
   188	    min_trial_drop = float(th.get("min_trial_recall_max_drop", 0.15))
   189	    refuted_rise = float(th.get("refuted_share_max_rise", 0.10))
   190	    bs = th.get("bootstrap") or {}
   191	    iterations = int(bs.get("iterations", 2000))
   192	    level = float(bs.get("level", 0.90))
   193	
   194	    planned_fx, planned_arms, manifests = set(), [], []
   195	    arms = {}
   196	    for batch in sorted(os.listdir(sdir)) if os.path.isdir(sdir) else []:
   197	        bdir = os.path.join(sdir, batch)
   198	        mp = os.path.join(bdir, "MANIFEST.json")
   199	        if not os.path.isfile(mp):
   200	            continue
   201	        m = json.load(open(mp, encoding="utf-8"))
   202	        if m.get("dry_run"):
   203	            continue
   204	        manifests.append(m)
   205	        planned_fx.update(m.get("fixtures") or [])
   206	        for a in m.get("arms") or []:
   207	            if a not in planned_arms:
   208	                planned_arms.append(a)
   209	            arm = arms.setdefault(a, Arm(a))
   210	            for row in read_jsonl(os.path.join(bdir, a, "results.jsonl")):
   211	                arm.add(row)
   212	    order = [a for a in arm_meta if a in arms] + [a for a in planned_arms if a not in arm_meta]
   213	    state = status.get("state", "unknown")
   214	    complete = state == "complete"
   215

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/cycle-ratio.sh: the two release-notes lines of a cycle, task-kind
     4	# counts and the volume ratio (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-10.3, PRD FR-10).
     5	#
     6	#   kinds: mechanical N · judgment N · operator N
     7	#   volume: script lines changed N (*.sh *.py *.ts *.js) · prose bytes changed N (*.md) · model calls N (MODELINV rows between the two commits' timestamps) · scope: host · modelinv: <path>
     8	#
     9	# Mapping (the glossary's "Kind counts" and "Volume ratio" entries):
    10	#   kinds          the 'kind: <value>' token that ends each top-level '- [ ]' /
    11	#                  '- [x]' task line under '### Technical Tasks', and each
    12	#                  '- [ ] Task ...' line under a '### Task N.E2E' heading, inside
    13	#                  a '## Sprint N' block of the sprint plan (fenced code skipped,
    14	#                  the same scope validate-artifact.sh --type sprint enforces);
    15	#                  untagged task lines are counted in --json and WARNed
    16	#   script lines   added + deleted lines of *.sh *.py *.ts *.js files between
    17	#                  the two commits (git diff --numstat, renames detected,
    18	#                  binary files skipped)
    19	#   prose bytes    bytes of the added and removed *.md lines between the two
    20	#                  commits, newline included, diff markers excluded
    21	#   model calls    MODELINV rows (primitive_id MODELINV) in the MODELINV log
    22	#                  whose ts_utc lies between the two commits' committer
    23	#                  timestamps, both ends included. The log is host-local, so
    24	#                  the count covers only the calls made on this host: "scope:
    25	#                  host". A missing log prints "model calls n/a" and a WARN.
    26	#
    27	# Git runs in the current directory's repository; --sprint-plan and --modelinv
    28	# default to paths under its top level.
    29	#
    30	# Usage:
    31	#   tools/cycle-ratio.sh --from SHA --to SHA [--sprint-plan PATH]
    32	#                        [--modelinv PATH] [--json]
    33	#
    34	#   --sprint-plan PATH  default grimoires/loa/sprint.md
    35	#   --modelinv PATH     default .run/model-invoke.jsonl
    36	#   --json              one JSON object instead of the two lines
    37	#
    38	# Exit 2 also covers: not a git repository, an unreadable sprint plan, jq missing.
    39	# Exit codes: 0 printed · 2 usage or unreadable input · 3 a SHA names no commit
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die() { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $2" >&2; exit "$1"; }
    46	
    47	SCRIPT_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    48	FENCE_AWK="$SCRIPT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/md-fence.awk"

    50	FROM=""
    51	TO=""
    52	PLAN=""

    56	  case "$1" in
    57	    --from|--to|--sprint-plan|--modelinv)
    58	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: $1 needs a value" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    59	      case "$1" in
    60	        --from) FROM="$2" ;;
    61	        --to) TO="$2" ;;
    62	        --sprint-plan) PLAN="$2" ;;
    63	        --modelinv) MODELINV="$2" ;;
    64	      esac
    65	      shift 2 ;;
    66	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    67	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    68	    *) echo "cycle-ratio.sh: unknown argument $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
    69	  esac
    70	done
    71	
    72	[[ -n "$FROM" && -n "$TO" ]] || { echo "cycle-ratio.sh: --from and --to are required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    73	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die 2 "jq is required"

    81	case "$FROM" in -*) die 3 "unknown commit: $FROM" ;; esac

   107	' "$PLAN")"

   109	[[ "$K_UNTAGGED" -eq 0 ]] || echo "WARN: $K_UNTAGGED task line(s) in $PLAN carry no kind: tag and are not counted" >&2

   111	# --- volume ------------------------------------------------------------------
   112	GIT_DIFF=(git -c core.quotePath=false diff --no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv -M)
   113	SCRIPT_LINES="$("${GIT_DIFF[@]}" --numstat "$FROM_SHA" "$TO_SHA" -- '*.sh' '*.py' '*.ts' '*.js' \
   114	  | awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { s += $1 + $2 } END { printf "%d\n", s }')"

   118	      /^@@ / { hunk = 1; next }
   119	      # the marker byte stands in for the newline the diff line drops
   120	      hunk && /^[+-]/ { s += length($0) }
   121	      END { printf "%d\n", s }
   122	    ')"
   123	
   124	# --- model calls -------------------------------------------------------------
   125	FROM_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$FROM_SHA")"
   126	TO_TS="$(git show -s --format=%ct "$TO_SHA")"
   127	MODEL_CALLS=""

   133	      | select(. != null and . >= $lo and . <= $hi)
   134	    ' "$MODELINV" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
   135	else

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""arms-report.py — the cycle-129 FR-2 control-arm report (SDD D-2.3).
     3	
     4	Invoked by `report.sh --arms`. Reads <results-root>/<suite>/STATUS.json (the
     5	suite aggregate run-arms.sh writes), every batch's MANIFEST.json and
     6	<arm>/results.jsonl, and the suite's pre-registered `ab.threshold` and
     7	`ab.arms`, and writes one markdown report.
     8	
     9	Per arm: recall (mean over defect fixtures of the per-fixture trial mean;
    10	the min, max and spread of the per-trial means), refuted share (cited
    11	findings matching neither a feedback label nor a fix region, over cited
    12	findings, pooled over completed trials), tokens per call, the percentile
    13	bootstrap interval of the recall drop (baseline - arm) resampling fixtures,
    14	the verdict and the missed labels.
    15	
    16	Verdict (pre-registered; never computed for baseline):
    17	  inconclusive  --partial; the run is not complete; a planned fixture lacks
    18	                trials_required completed trials in the arm or the baseline;
    19	                model or source skew; no defect fixture; or only a recall
    20	                rule is violated while the mean drop does not exceed the
    21	                baseline's own trial-to-trial spread (a change too small to name)
    22	  recall loss   the refuted-share rule is violated, or a recall rule is
    23	                violated and the mean drop exceeds the baseline spread
    24	  no recall loss  every rule holds:
    25	                  upper bound of the drop interval <= mean_recall_max_drop
    26	                  arm min trial mean >= baseline min trial mean - min_trial_recall_max_drop
    27	                  arm refuted share <= baseline refuted share + refuted_share_max_rise
    28	An `informational: true` arm's verdict reports a yield only.
    29	
    30	Exit: 0 written, 1 refused (a suite is not complete and --partial was not
    31	given), 2 error. Stdlib only.
    32	"""

    34	import datetime
    35	import json
    36	import os
    37	import random
    38	import sys

    49	def read_jsonl(path):
    50	    rows = []
    51	    if not os.path.isfile(path):

    53	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:

    63	
    64	def mean(xs):

    67	
    68

    71	
    72

content.content:
# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

---

## Architecture Rubrics

### ARCH-MO: Modularity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Clear separation of concerns. Well-defined interfaces. Easy to modify/extend. |
| 4 | Good modularity with minor coupling issues. |
| 3 | Some modularity but tight coupling in places. |
| 2 | Poor separation. Components heavily interdependent. |
| 1 | Monolithic. No clear boundaries. |

### ARCH-SC: Scalability
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Horizontally scalable. Stateless services. Caching strategy. Database sharding ready. |
| 4 | Mostly scalable with minor bottlenecks. |
| 3 | Can scale vertically but horizontal scaling problematic. |
| 2 | Scalability issues. Single points of failure. |
---OUTPUT-SCHEMA---
# Structured Finding Output Schema

Defines the JSONL output format for machine-parseable audit findings.

## Finding Schema

Each finding is a JSON object on a single line in the JSONL file.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "title": "AuditFinding",
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["id", "category", "criterion", "severity", "score", "finding", "reasoning_trace", "confidence"],
  "properties": {
    "id": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^[A-Z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}$",
      "description": "Unique finding ID (e.g., SEC-001, ARCH-042)"
    },
    "category": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["security", "architecture", "code_quality", "devops", "blockchain"],
      "description": "Audit category"
    },
    "criterion": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Specific rubric dimension (e.g., input_validation, modularity)"
    },
    "severity": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["CRITICAL", "HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW", "INFO"],
      "description": "Finding severity"
    },
    "score": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1,
      "maximum": 5,
      "description": "Rubric score for this dimension"
    },
    "file": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "File path where issue was found"
    },
    "line": {
      "type": "integer",
      "description": "Line number (if applicable)"
    },
    "code_snippet": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Relevant code excerpt"
    },
    "reasoning_trace": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "How the issue was discovered - analysis path and evidence"
    },
    "finding": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "Clear description of the issue"
    },

# Sprint 1 Security Audit

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md (task review-r19)
**Change under audit:** `pr/head.diff` — feat(cycle-129): sprint-255 — guard register with origin and yield, pre-registered control arms on a record corpus, task kinds, path-scoped rule files (81 files)
**Review feedback:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md (CHANGES_REQUIRED, 0 critical / 1 high / 5 medium / 9 low, excluded 0)
**Dissent envelope:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-audit.json (primary `gpt-5.5-pro` via codex-headless: clean; companion `claude-headless`: 1 MEDIUM, 4 LOW; 0 rejected payloads; `degraded: false`)
**Methodology:** Systematic 5-category review (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps; Blockchain n/a)

---

## Prerequisite deviation

The audit skill's Phase 0 requires `engineer-feedback.md` to say "All good". It says CHANGES REQUIRED. The task directive for review-r19 orders the audit to run regardless and to write this file, so the audit proceeded; the review's one HIGH is re-examined below rather than assumed. No `COMPLETED` marker is written. Guardrails pre-check: `PROCEED`. Beads (`br`) is not installed; no bead comment or label was recorded.

## Scope limits

- The fixture holds the 81 touched files only. `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, the eight record fixtures under `evals/fixtures/review-prs/pr-11…pr-18`, their hidden labels, `SHA256SUMS`, `evals/harness/sandbox.sh`, `grade.sh`, `no-secrets.sh` and `tools/check-prompt-budget.sh` are not present and could not be audited. Nothing below claims a defect in them.
- `run-arms.bats` and `seed-corpus.bats` were not executed (they need the absent helpers); the HIGH below was confirmed by tracing the code path, not by running it.
- No `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-*.md` exists for this sprint; the documentation check below was done by hand against the diff.

---

## Executive Summary

The change adds a guard register generated from the repository (`guard-yield.sh`, `guard-origins.yaml`, `floor.yaml`), a control-arm driver and report for the review/audit recall evals (`run-arms.sh`, `arms-report.py`, arm toggles in `execute-agent.sh`), a seeder that turns shipped sprints into record fixtures (`seed-corpus-from-record.sh`), a `kind:` task tag validator, and `paths:` frontmatter on two rule files. Input handling across the new scripts is good: every id, batch name, commit, model and fixture argument is regex-gated, YAML lookups go through `strenv`, JSON through `--arg`/`--argjson`, Python runs with `-I`, and the yield writer leaks no command text, cwd or model name (GY-5). No hardcoded secret, injection path or privilege escalation was found.

One finding blocks. `run-arms.sh` admits a second run into a batch that already holds results for the same source commit and model, re-plans every trial, appends duplicate rows to `<arm>/results.jsonl`, overwrites per-trial artifacts and restarts the STATUS counters at zero. `arms-report.py` counts every row, so the pre-registered verdict that may license deleting a guard can be computed over duplicated trials while STATUS.json reads `complete`. The default batch name is deterministic, so a re-run after the documented `partial` exit lands exactly here. The review found this; the audit confirms it independently as HIGH (data-integrity of a safety-relevant decision input, CWE-345).

Five MEDIUMs follow: the floor pins guard identifiers but not the fence body or the deny list that implements two thirds of the floor guards; `guard-yield.sh` sources the heredoc classifier into its own process; `implementing-tasks/SKILL.md` widens its app-zone permission with no rationale; `stash-safety.md` becomes conditional on the files in play; and `run-arms.sh` uses a GNU-only `date` form that fails every trial on the BSD platform its own comments claim to support. Eleven LOWs are listed. The review's trailer excludes no high, so `excluded_confirmed` is 0.

**Overall Risk Level:** MODERATE

**Key Statistics:**

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 5 |
| Low | 11 |

---

## Category Scores (Rubric-Based Assessment)

**Scoring Method:** Each dimension scored 1-5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md`

| Category | Score | Dimensions |
|----------|-------|------------|
| Security | 4.0/5 | IV:4 AZ:4 CI:4 IN:5 AV:3 |
| Architecture | 3.8/5 | MO:4 SC:4 RE:3 CX:4 ST:4 |
| Code Quality | 3.8/5 | RD:4 TC:4 EH:3 TS:4 DC:4 |
| DevOps | 3.6/5 | AU:4 OB:4 RC:3 AC:4 DS:3 |
| Blockchain | n/a | not applicable |
| **Overall** | **3.8/5** | *Security weighted highest* |

**Machine-Parseable Output:** `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/2026-10-21/findings.jsonl`

---

## Critical Issues (Fix Immediately)

None.

---

## High Priority Issues (Fix Before Production)

### [HIGH-001] Control-arm driver re-runs a batch in place: duplicate trial rows feed the pre-registered verdict

**Severity:** HIGH | **Confidence:** high
**Component:** `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:251-257` (admission), `:126` (deterministic default batch), `:264-265` (counters restart at 0), `:408` (rows appended), `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:135`, `:239` (every row is a cell)
**Criterion:** SEC-AV / ARCH-RE (integrity of a decision input)

**Reasoning Trace:**
> `run-arms.sh:126` builds the default batch as `batch-${FIXTURES[0]}-${FIXTURES[last]}-n${#FIXTURES[@]}`, a pure function of the fixture list. The pre-flight at `:251-256` reads the existing MANIFEST.json and dies only when `prev_src != SRC_FULL || prev_model != MODEL`; with the same pair it falls through to `write_manifest` at `:257`, which overwrites MANIFEST.json. `PLAN` is rebuilt from scratch at `:160-165`, `DONE`/`FAILED` are zeroed at `:265`, and `collect()` appends each new row with `>>` at `:408` without reading what the file already holds. `keep_artifacts` at `:387` writes to `trial-$4$5`, the same path as the previous run, so artifacts are overwritten while both rows survive. `arms-report.py:135` appends every completed row to `cells[fx]`; `coverage_gaps` at `:239` counts `len(arm.cells[fx])`, so duplicates satisfy `trials_required`. The exit contract at `:41-43` ("1 partial … results kept") invites exactly this re-run. `run-arms.bats` RA-3 (`:110`, `:123`) re-runs only with fresh `--batch` names, and RA-5 (`:144`) covers only the different-model refusal; no test exercises a same-batch re-run.

**Description:** A second invocation with the same source commit and model on an existing batch is admitted, duplicates every (arm, fixture, trial) cell, breaks the row/artifact pairing and resets the per-arm counters, so STATUS.json and `results.jsonl` describe different experiments.

**Impact:** `arms-report.py` is the gate that licenses removing a control (SDD D-2.3). After a re-run, `fixture_means` and `trial_means` are biased toward whichever run was duplicated, `trials done` exceeds `trials_planned`, the missed-label counts double, and STATUS.json still reads `complete`. A guard deletion could be justified by a verdict computed over duplicated data. Unlikely to be adversarial, but the failure is silent and the default path leads straight into it.

**Proof of Concept:**
```
run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_rule_files --fixtures pr-11,pr-12 --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
# one trial fails twice -> exit 1 "partial"; operator re-runs the same command to fill the gap
run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_rule_files --fixtures pr-11,pr-12 --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
# admitted (same source/model); baseline/results.jsonl now holds 2 rows per cell; STATUS trials_done counts only run 2
```

**Remediation:** Either refuse a batch whose `<arm>/results.jsonl` already exists (same shape and message as `:255`, "use another --batch"), or implement a real resume: read existing rows, skip cells that already hold a `completed` row, seed `DONE`/`FAILED` from them and keep MANIFEST.json. Add an RA test that re-runs the same batch and asserts one row per (arm, fixture, trial).

**References:** CWE-345 Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/345.html ; CWE-1288 Improper Validation of Consistency within Input — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1288.html

---

## Medium Priority Issues (Address in Next Sprint)

### [MED-001] The floor pins guard identifiers, not the code that implements most floor guards

**Severity:** MEDIUM | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:46-50` (floor_files), `:42` (`implement_gate.*` floor key), `head/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml:163` (`hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh` floor: false), `:208` and `:810` (implement-gate rows floor: false), `:884` (`policy:permission-deny-list` script is `settings.deny.json`)
**Criterion:** SEC-AZ / DEVOPS-RC

**Description:** Sixteen of the twenty-one `floor_guards` are `fence:FR-SZ*` and `fence:FR-1.2b` rows implemented only by `block-destructive-bash.sh` and armed by the `PreToolUse:Bash` registration. `floor_files` pins neither the fence nor `.claude/settings.json`. `floor-snapshot.bats` FS-3 pins the hook registrations and FS-4 pins the ordered `emit_block`/`pattern_id` call-site list, and `floor_corpus` pins the expected verdict of the existing corpus rows, so removing a guard or a registration is caught. A new allow branch inside the fence body (another env-var bypass, a widened `_c2_authorized` check) changes no call site and is exercised by no existing corpus row, so it passes every floor suite while the register still prints `floor: yes`. Likewise `policy:permission-deny-list` is enforced by `permissions.deny` in `.claude/settings.json` (62 entries on this host), which is not pinned; `settings.deny.json` is the template. And `implement_gate.*` is a floor key while both implement-gate rows are `floor: false`. Raised by the review and by the companion dissent (DISS-C-001).

**Impact:** A cycle task can weaken a floor guard's behaviour without any floor test going red; the floor's documented promise ("no profile, knob or cycle task may weaken") is narrower than its wording.

**Remediation:** Add `.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh` to `floor_files` (or pin its sha in `guard-origins.bats` beside the floor.yaml pin and bump deliberately), diff `.claude/settings.json` `permissions.deny` against `settings.deny.json` in FS-3, and make `floor_keys` and the `floor:` rows agree on implement-gate.

**References:** CWE-693 Protection Mechanism Failure — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html

### [MED-002] guard-yield.sh sources the heredoc classifier into its own process

**Severity:** MEDIUM | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:468-470`
**Criterion:** CQ-EH

**Description:** `source "$HEREDOC_LIB"` runs the library in the generator's shell. The live `heredoc-classifier.sh` sources the fence with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` (lib line 19), so the head state works, but a lib whose fence does not honour library mode runs the fence as a hook and ends `guard-yield.sh` with exit 0 and nothing written (observed by the review on a composite root). `--check` exits before this section and cannot detect it.

**Impact:** A silent no-op generation that reports success; the yield files go stale without a signal.

**Remediation:** Call `heredoc_nonexec` through a subshell (`( source "$HEREDOC_LIB"; heredoc_nonexec "$cmd" )`), or probe the lib in a subshell first and treat a missing summary line as exit 3.

**References:** CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

### [MED-003] implementing-tasks app-zone permission widened without rationale

**Severity:** MEDIUM | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:28`
**Criterion:** SEC-AZ

**Description:** `zones.app.permission` changes from `read` to `read-write`. The PR title names the guard register, control arms, task kinds and path-scoped rule files; this hunk is none of them and the diff carries no comment, DEC row or test. `/implement` is the sanctioned writer of app code, so the value is probably a correction, but it is a security-relevant declaration moving silently. `reviewing-code/SKILL.md:135` now points at the frontmatter `zones:` as the zone source, which raises the weight of that key. Raised by the review and the companion dissent (DISS-C-003).

**Impact:** Any future consumer of `zones.app.permission` inherits an unaudited grant; a later audit cannot distinguish it from drift.

**Remediation:** Add a one-line rationale (or DEC row) and a bats assertion that only `implementing-tasks` carries `app: read-write`.

**References:** CWE-250 Execution with Unnecessary Privileges — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/250.html

### [MED-004] stash-safety.md becomes conditional on which files are edited

**Severity:** MEDIUM | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2-6`
**Criterion:** SEC-AV (prose guard coverage)

**Description:** The new `paths:` globs (`**/*.sh`, `**/*.bats`, `.claude/scripts/**`, `.claude/hooks/**`) load the rule only when a shell file is in play, but `git stash push/pop` is typed into Bash regardless of the files being edited. In an app-code session only the harness regex FR-1.2b remains, and it fires only on the swallowed-output shape. `rule-paths.bats` attributes the globs to SDD D-3.1 / DEC-0129, so this is a recorded decision; recorded here as residual risk. Raised by the review and the companion dissent (DISS-C-005).

**Impact:** A plain `git stash push && … && git stash pop` while editing Python or Markdown runs without the rule in context and without a fence.

**Remediation:** Record in the DEC row that the fence, not the prose, is the only stash guard outside shell sessions, or widen the globs.

### [MED-005] GNU-only millisecond clock breaks every trial on BSD/macOS

**Severity:** MEDIUM | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:326`, `:366`, `:374`
**Criterion:** DEVOPS-DS

**Description:** `date +%s%N | cut -c1-13` relies on GNU `%N`; BSD `date` prints a literal `N`, so `start_ms` is `1729500000N` and `$(( end_ms - start_ms ))` at `:374` is an arithmetic error inside the background job under `set -e`. No row is written and `collect()` records `FAILED (no row written)` for every trial. The script's own comment at `:263` claims bash 3.2 (macOS) compatibility.

**Impact:** A whole batch fails on the platform the script says it supports; the failure mode looks like an executor problem.

**Remediation:** `python3 -c 'import time;print(int(time.time()*1000))'` (python3 is already required at `:95`), or seconds via `date +%s`.

---

## Low Priority Issues (Technical Debt)

### [LOW-001] Replay flag is taken on trust from the environment

**Severity:** LOW | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:528-529`, `:782`, `:1367`, `:1520`; `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:337`; `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:499`
**Description:** Four audit-row writers stamp `replay: true` whenever `LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY == "1"`; nothing ties the flag to the corpus runner. `guard-yield.sh:499` excludes flagged rows from the 30-day yield. If the variable leaks into an interactive Claude Code session (a `settings.json` `env` block, a shell profile, a leftover export from a corpus run), real blocks disappear from the yield that operators read to judge whether a guard earns its keep. The burst rule at `:518-519` has the same shape: ten blocks in one UTC minute hide all ten. Raised by the companion dissent (DISS-C-002). Low because the yield is advisory and the heuristics are documented in the header.
**Remediation:** Have the replaying suites write to a separate audit log (`LOA_REPO_ROOT` already points them at a scratch root), or key the flag on a nonce the runner alone holds; report `replay_rows_by_rule.flag` in the `/loa` Guards line so a non-zero count outside a test run is visible.
**References:** CWE-807 Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html

### [LOW-002] Transport-failure heuristic reads the model's own text

**Severity:** LOW | **Confidence:** medium
**Component:** `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:314-315`
**Description:** `is_transport_failure` greps `agent-output.json` (the result text) for `network` and `5[0-9][0-9] `; a review that mentions a network call or a line number followed by a space classifies a genuine agent error as transport and spends the single retry.
**Remediation:** Match the stderr log and the structured `api_error_status` / `subtype` fields only.

### [LOW-003] Unquoted `find` and unvalidated `--results-dir`

**Severity:** LOW | **Confidence:** high

**Criterion:** SEC-AV / ARCH-RE (integrity of a decision input)

**Reasoning Trace:**
> `run-arms.sh:126` builds the default batch as `batch-${FIXTURES[0]}-${FIXTURES[last]}-n${#FIXTURES[@]}`, a pure function of the fixture list. The pre-flight at `:251-256` reads the existing MANIFEST.json and dies only when `prev_src != SRC_FULL || prev_model != MODEL`; with the same pair it falls through to `write_manifest` at `:257`, which overwrites MANIFEST.json. `PLAN` is rebuilt from scratch at `:160-165`, `DONE`/`FAILED` are zeroed at `:265`, and `collect()` appends each new row with `>>` at `:408` without reading what the file already holds. `keep_artifacts` at `:387` writes to `trial-$4$5`, the same path as the previous run, so artifacts are overwritten while both rows survive. `arms-report.py:135` appends every completed row to `cells[fx]`; `coverage_gaps` at `:239` counts `len(arm.cells[fx])`, so duplicates satisfy `trials_required`. **Description:** A second invocation with the same source commit and model on an existing batch is admitted, duplicates every (arm, fixture, trial) cell, breaks the row/artifact pairing and resets the per-arm counters, so STATUS.json and `results.jsonl` describe different experiments.

**Impact:** `arms-report.py` is the gate that licenses removing a control (SDD D-2.3). After a re-run, `fixture_means` and `trial_means` are biased toward whichever run was duplicated, `trials done` exceeds `trials_planned`, the missed-label counts double, and STATUS.json still reads `complete`. A guard deletion could be justified by a verdict computed over duplicated data. Unlikely to be adversarial, but the failure is silent and the default path leads straight into it.

**Proof of Concept:**
```
run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_rule_files --fixtures pr-11,pr-12 --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
# one trial fails twice -> exit 1 "partial"; operator re-runs the same command to fill the gap
run-arms.sh --suite review-recall --arms baseline,no_rule_files --fixtures pr-11,pr-12 --trials 3 --source-commit <sha>
# admitted (same source/model); baseline/results.jsonl now holds 2 rows per cell; STATUS trials_done counts only run 2
```

**Remediation:** Either refuse a batch whose `<arm>/results.jsonl` already exists (same shape and message as `:255`, "use another --batch"), or implement a real resume: read existing rows, skip cells that already hold a `completed` row, seed `DONE`/`FAILED` from them and keep MANIFEST.json. **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** for sprint-1 (PR sprint-255, 81 files). Feedback is at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`, and verdict-derive reports it consistent with the review trailer (exit 0, no violations). No COMPLETED marker was created.

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 5 |
| Low | 11 |

**The blocking finding** is the one the review raised, confirmed independently by tracing the code path. The control-arm driver admits a second run into a batch with the same source commit and model, appends duplicate trial rows, resets its counters and overwrites artifacts. The report script counts every row, so the pre-registered verdict that can license deleting a guard may be computed over duplicated data while STATUS reads complete. The default batch name is deterministic, so the documented "partial, re-run" path leads straight into it. No test covers a same-batch re-run.

**Mediums** cover the floor pinning gap (the fence body and the live deny list are not pinned, only call sites and registrations), the heredoc classifier being sourced in-process, the unexplained app-zone permission widening in the implementing-tasks skill, the path-scoped stash rule, and a GNU-only clock that fails every trial on macOS.

**New beyond the review** are two lows from the companion dissent that I verified: the replay flag on audit rows is trusted straight from the environment, so a leaked variable hides real blocks from the yield, and the reviewer prompt lost its inline red-flag list.

**Deviations to note.** The review verdict was CHANGES_REQUIRED rather than "All good", so the skill's prerequisite was not met; I proceeded under the task directive and recorded that in the report. Beads is not installed, so no bead comment was written. Several helpers named by the PR (sandbox, grader, no-secrets, the prompt-budget tool, the record corpus) are outside the fixture and are listed as scope limits.

Supporting artifacts: dissent envelope at `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-audit.json` (primary voice clean, companion five findings, zero rejected), structured findings at `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/2026-10-21/findings.jsonl`, trajectory log and NOTES.md session entry updated.
